articles.summary: 3D Systems Opens New Industrial Technology Center to Expand America's Advanced Manufacturing Capacity Elizabeth Piet Wed, 10/21/2026 - 15:30 Release Date Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026 4:54 PM New Colorado facility strengthens domestic 3D printing production capabilities for aerospace, defense, and semiconductor equipment manufacturers while advancing supply chain resilience Adds 50,000 sq. foot of production and office space at Littleton, CO. campus Increases opportunities for workforce development in Colorado region From Left: Joe Zuiker, 3D Systems. Reji Puthenveetil, 3D Systems. Representative Sheila Lieder, Colorado Assembly. U.S. Representative Brittany Pettersen. Jeff Graves, CEO, 3D Systems. US Senator John Hickenlooper. Phyllis Nordstrom, 3D Systems. Merrill Stillwell, Councilmember City of Littleton​, CO. Trista Borrego​, Littleton CO. Business Chamber. ROCK HILL, South Carolina, October 21, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) today announced the grand opening of its new Industrial Technology Center in Littleton, Colorado, expanding the company's ability to help aerospace, defense, and semiconductor equipment manufacturers accelerate the development, qualification, and production of mission-critical components using 3D printing. The addition of approximately 50,000 square feet of manufacturing and office space increases the 3D Systems’ advanced manufacturing capacity to approximately 270,000 square feet across Europe and US, creating one of the industry’s most comprehensive additive manufacturing offerings. The expanded facility in Colorado strengthens domestic manufacturing capacity, enhances supply chain resilience, and supports growing demand for qualified U.S.-based production. "Customers today need more than manufacturing capacity. They need a trusted partner that can help them develop applications, qualify processes, and scale production with confidence," said Reji Puthenveetil, Executive Vice President, Additive Solutions, 3D Systems. "The expansion of our Littleton campus allows us to rapidly scale production while leveraging the same validated processes, quality systems, and manufacturing expertise that customers depend upon for their most critical applications." Supporting America's Industrial Base The Littleton campus now serves as a strategic hub for customers seeking to accelerate adoption of additive manufacturing while reducing development risk and shortening time to production. The expansion reflects increasing demand for domestic manufacturing solutions across aerospace, defense, and semiconductor equipment markets, where secure supply chains, production readiness, and manufacturing flexibility are becoming increasingly important. Combined with the company's expertise in additive manufacturing hardware, materials, software, and application engineering, the facility provides customers with a pathway from concept development through qualified production. Built for Qualified Production The Littleton facility maintains certifications and registrations required to support highly regulated and mission-critical applications, including: ISO9001 / AS9100D Certified ITAR Registered JCP Registered / eJCP in-process (DD2345s) CMMC Level 2 compliant (CUI) These capabilities enable customers to move more efficiently from application development and qualification to repeatable, production-scale manufacturing. Expanding from a Proven Foundation The Industrial Technology Center builds upon decades of manufacturing experience in regulated healthcare applications. The Littleton campus has developed extensive expertise in process validation, quality management, and production of highly demanding applications, capabilities that are increasingly valuable to aerospace, defense, and semiconductor customers. "The opening of the Industrial Technology Center not only expands our industrial manufacturing capabilities but also creates additional opportunities for the continued growth of our healthcare manufacturing operations," said Dr. Jeffrey Graves, President and CEO of 3D Systems. "This investment reinforces our commitment to advanced manufacturing in the United States while creating new opportunities for engineers, technicians, and manufacturing professionals in Colorado." Creating a Unique Domestic Additive Manufacturing Ecosystem Upon completion of planned investments, 3D Systems will offer one of the industry's most comprehensive domestic metal additive manufacturing ecosystems, encompassing: Metal additive system development in California of the multi-phase U.S. Air Force sponsored program Large-format printer manufacturing in South Carolina Application development, qualification, and certified parts production in Colorado This integrated approach positions the company to support customers seeking secure, domestic supply chains while accelerating the adoption of advanced manufacturing technologies. "With validated facilities, certified quality systems, advanced applications expertise, and scalable production capacity already in place, we are uniquely positioned to help customers move from concept to qualified production faster and with less risk," said Dr. Graves. "Our goal is simple: help customers innovate more quickly while strengthening the resilience of critical American manufacturing supply chains." About 3D Systems For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; AI infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com . articles.summary: NextDent 3D Printing Materials for 18 3D Printing Systems Chelsie Keeler Fri, 10/16/2026 - 14:05 Portfolio of NextDent 3D printing materials for dental applications. The Printer You Have, The Materials You Need: NextDent 3D Printing Materials for Your Existing Equipment Digital dentistry continues to evolve rapidly with new 3D printers, materials, and workflows entering the market all the time, giving dental labs and clinics more opportunities to improve productivity and expand the services they offer. But adopting new capabilities doesn’t always have to mean investing in new equipment but rather adding better solutions to existing technology. With NextDent® 3D printing materials from 3D Systems, labs and clinics may be able to get more from the printers they already have. The NextDent material portfolio is validated across a wide range of dental 3D printing platforms, giving users greater flexibility to access high-quality dental materials without replacing their existing hardware. More Material Choice Across More Printing Platforms NextDent materials support a broad range of 3D printed dental applications, including models, trays, surgical guides, orthodontic appliances, dentures, crown and bridge, castings and more. These materials have been validated for use beyond 3D Systems hardware, including 3D printers from Asiga, Phrozen, Formlabs, Prusa, Shining3D, Axtra3D, DMG and RayShape. This flexibility can make a meaningful difference for a lab or clinic that has already invested in digital dentistry. Instead of starting with the question, “What new printer do we need?” organizations can first ask, “What more can we do with the equipment we already have?” Protect Your Existing Equipment Investment A 3D printer represents a significant investment, not only in the hardware itself, but also in training and workflow development. Replacing a working printer simply to gain access to a different material can add unnecessary cost and disruption. By validating NextDent materials on a variety of industry-leading dental 3D printers, 3D Systems is helping lower that barrier to adoption. 3D Systems specifically identifies broader printer compatibility as a way for more 3D printing solutions to take advantage of the NextDent material portfolio. For labs and clinics, that can mean the opportunity to expand material choices or introduce new applications while continuing to utilize existing equipment. It can also help organizations with multiple printer brands across their operation. A broader material portfolio gives teams the opportunity to evaluate materials based on the application and desired result rather than being limited solely by the name on the front of the printer. Quality Without Starting Over NextDent brings decades of dental material expertise to digital workflows, with materials designed for applications ranging from highly accurate models and surgical guides to dentures and permanent restorations. The NextDent portfolio includes CE-certified and biocompatible materials developed specifically for dental applications. For labs and clinics, this creates an opportunity to pair equipment they already know with materials engineered specifically for dentistry, helping maximize existing investments while continuing to pursue reliable, repeatable results. Before purchasing another printer, take a closer look at what your current equipment can already do. With NextDent materials validated across a growing range of 3D printing platforms, the path to a new application, expanded capacity or a more versatile digital workflow may already be sitting in your lab. Get more from the equipment you already own. Explore the NextDent material portfolio and find the validated materials available for your 3D printer. articles.summary: Precision Resource Breaks Ground on Two New Production Additive Manufacturing Facilities and Expands Value-Added Services in Partnership with 3D Systems Elizabeth Piet Wed, 10/28/2026 - 15:07 Release Date Wednesday, Oct 28, 2026 4:30 PM Precision Resource expands U.S. production metal additive manufacturing footprint with new locations in California and Connecticut Expands Precision Resource's additive manufacturing network and supports a more integrated manufacturing solution for commercial and defense customers Deploys 3D Systems' metal additive manufacturing technology to expand production capacity, accelerate production at scale, and support long-term growth ROCK HILL, South Carolina, and SHELTON, Conn. October 28, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE:DDD) and Precision Resource , a leader in the production of critical components for the automotive, heavy-duty, aerospace, and medical device industries, today announced the groundbreaking of two new additive manufacturing locations, one in Huntington Beach, California, and one in Shelton, Connecticut. Precision Resource will further add in-house heat treatment and expand its complex machining capabilities, giving commercial and defense customers a more integrated path from 3D printed part to finished component. The facilities will utilize advanced metal additive manufacturing systems from 3D Systems and are expected to be operational in Q1 2027, a milestone that coincides with Precision Resource's 80th year in business. In Huntington Beach, California, Precision Resource is breaking ground on its second additive manufacturing location. This expansion will double the site’s current industrial additive manufacturing capacity. In Shelton, Connecticut, the company is breaking ground on its first additive manufacturing location that can further expand as demand grows. Together, the Huntington Beach and Shelton investments expand Precision Resource's additive manufacturing ecosystem and strengthen its partnership with 3D Systems, creating a connected manufacturing network across both locations. The expansion positions Precision Resource to significantly increase production capacity while creating one of the most comprehensive metal additive manufacturing networks in North America, supporting growing demand from commercial and defense customers. "This expansion is much more than adding machines. We are building something significant by connecting our Huntington Beach and Shelton operations into an integrated additive manufacturing network," said Chris Gratton, Director of Additive and Machine Operations at Precision Resource. "Together, these operations give our customers greater capacity, flexibility, and a faster path from print to finished component. They also allow us to reduce supply-chain complexity, provide greater manufacturing and geographic redundancy, and take on increasingly demanding production programs with the speed, quality and reliability our customers require." Precision Resource is expanding its additive manufacturing capabilities with the addition of 3D Systems' DMP Flex 350 Triple metal 3D printing technology. These new machines add to the fleet of DMP 350 systems already in operation at Precision Resource, further expanding a proven additive manufacturing platform that has supported the company's growth in production applications across commercial and defense markets. The platform combines high-throughput production with exceptional part quality and repeatability, helping Precision Resource meet growing demand for complex, production-grade metal components across commercial and defense markets. "Precision Resource has established itself as a leader in delivering high-quality, production-ready metal components to demanding markets," said Reji Puthenveetil, EVP, Additive Solutions and Chief Commercial Officer, 3D Systems. "This expansion demonstrates how additive manufacturing is increasingly becoming an integrated production solution for critical commercial and defense applications. By combining Precision Resource's manufacturing expertise with 3D Systems' advanced DMP technology and application expertise, these new facilities will help accelerate the adoption of high-volume, production-grade metal additive manufacturing for critical commercial and defense applications while providing customers with the scale, consistency, and reliability required for mission-critical programs." About Precision Resource Founded in 1947, Precision Resource is a global manufacturer of custom engineered metal components headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut. The company serves automotive, heavy duty, medical, semiconductor, commercial and defense markets with capabilities including fine blanking, grinding, lapping, laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing, heat treatment and complex machining. Learn more at www.precisionresource.com About 3D Systems For 40 years, Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials, and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com. articles.summary: 3D Systems Expands European Dental Presence Through Partnership with BioSummer Dental Elizabeth Piet Sat, 10/31/2026 - 13:49 Release Date Monday, Nov 2, 2026 7:40 AM BioSummer Dental adds NextDent® 300 MultiJet 3D printers to its distribution portfolio, supporting broader access to digital denture production across France. ROCK HILL, S.C., November 2, 2026 — 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) today announced an expansion of its long-standing strategic distribution partnership with BioSummer Dental, a France-based distributor of advanced digital dentistry solutions. As part of the collaboration, BioSummer Dental has added the NextDent 300 MultiJet 3D printer to its portfolio and is preparing to deliver the first units to several strategic customers, reinforcing its commitment to bringing innovative dental 3D printing technologies to laboratories throughout Europe. The expansion supports 3D Systems' European growth strategy following the achievement of EU Medical Device Regulation (EU MDR 2017/745) certification in April 2026 for the NextDent Jet Base and Teeth materials, enabling commercialization throughout the European Union. With this critical milestone achieved, the Company is now expanding market access through strategic distribution partnerships and helping more dental laboratories transition to efficient, scalable digital denture production. “Expanding our presence in Europe is a key priority for our dental business, and strong distribution partners like BioSummer Dental are essential to that growth,” said Jeff Graves, President and CEO of 3D Systems. “BioSummer Dental’s decision to add the NextDent 300 to its portfolio demonstrates their confidence in our technology and the opportunity ahead for digital denture production. We are pleased to strengthen this partnership as we work together to bring the benefits of the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution to more laboratories, and ultimately, more patients across Europe.” The NextDent Jetted Denture Solution enables laboratories to produce highly aesthetic, durable monolithic dentures through a streamlined, integrated workflow. By simplifying production and reducing labor-intensive manual processes, the solution helps laboratories improve efficiency, increase productivity, and consistently deliver high-quality, patient-specific dentures. Through its established presence in the dental industry and expertise in digital workflows, BioSummer Dental plays an important role in making these capabilities more accessible to dental professionals. The addition of the NextDent 300 positions BioSummer Dental to support broader adoption as laboratories seek more efficient solutions to meet growing production demands. “We are excited to expand our partnership with 3D Systems and add the NextDent 300 to our distribution portfolio,” said Olivier Bellaton, CEO, BioSummer Dental. “Digital denture production represents a significant opportunity for dental laboratories across Europe. We believe the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution offers an exceptional combination of quality, productivity, and ease of use, and we look forward to helping our customers take advantage of this technology.” Together, 3D Systems and BioSummer Dental aim to accelerate the adoption of digital denture workflows, making advanced manufacturing solutions more accessible to dental professionals across France and the rest of Europe. For more information about the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution, visit www.3dsystems.com/dental-jetted-dentures . As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com . About BioSummer Dental BioSummer Dental is a France-based provider and distributor of digital dental technologies and solutions. With a focus on helping dental professionals adopt innovative manufacturing workflows, the company offers technologies designed to support productivity, precision, and efficiency in modern dental laboratories. For more information, visit www.biosummer.com . articles.summary: 3D Systems Donates NextDent 300 3D Printer to Remote Area Medical to Expand Access to Free Denture Care in the U.S. Elizabeth Piet Thu, 10/29/2026 - 15:34 Release Date Thursday, Oct 29, 2026 3:34 PM Donation supports Remote Area Medical’s mission to bring high-quality dental care to underserved communities through advanced 3D printing technology. ROCK HILL, S.C., October 29, 2026 — 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) today announced the donation of a NextDent® 300 MultiJet 3D printer to Remote Area Medical (RAM®), a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing free, quality dental, vision, and medical care to underserved and uninsured individuals in the United States. The donation supports RAM’s mission to eliminate barriers to essential healthcare by expanding its ability to provide customized, high-quality dentures to patients in need, at no cost. For individuals without access to affordable dental care, missing teeth can significantly affect their ability to eat, speak, and engage confidently in everyday life. Yet the cost of restorative dental treatment, including dentures, can place these essential services out of reach. Since 1985, RAM has worked to eliminate these barriers, delivering free healthcare services to more than one million patients across the United States. In 2025 alone, the organization served 32,770 patients and provided more than $16.6 million in free healthcare through the efforts of over 17,000 volunteers. After learning about RAM’s mission and its use of 3D Systems’ NextDent 5100 platform to provide dentures for underserved patients, 3D Systems CEO Jeff Graves saw an opportunity to further support RAM’s efforts. The donation of the Company’s new NextDent 300 MultiJet 3D printer will help RAM expand its digital denture manufacturing capabilities, enabling faster production of high-quality dentures for patients in need. The NextDent 300, powered by 3D Systems’ MultiJet 3D Printing technology, enables the production of highly realistic, durable monolithic dentures, with teeth and gums printed together as a single piece. By streamlining traditionally labor-intensive denture manufacturing processes, the solution helps reduce production time while delivering the precision, fit, and natural aesthetics patients deserve. The donated printer system is now installed and operational at RAM’s facility in Knoxville, Tennessee, where the organization is already using the technology to produce dentures for members of the community. Once RAM’s newest mobile dental laboratory is completed, the NextDent 300 will be integrated into the mobile unit, expanding the organization’s ability to bring advanced digital denture production directly to underserved communities across the country. “Remote Area Medical has an extraordinary record of bringing essential healthcare to people who need it most,” said Jeff Graves, CEO of 3D Systems. “We are proud to support that work with the NextDent 300, which enables the production of high-quality monolithic dentures more efficiently. The ability to eat comfortably, speak clearly, and smile with confidence can have a profound impact on a person’s quality of life. We hope this donation helps RAM extend that impact to even more patients.” “A Mirror Moment lasts only a few seconds, but its impact lasts a lifetime. It’s the first time in years someone smiles without covering their mouth, with the confidence to apply for a job, share a meal with family, or simply laugh out loud. Remote Area Medical’s partnership with 3D Systems lets us give patients high-quality dentures, and with them, a moment many thought they’d never have again. Together, we’re proving what’s possible when innovation and compassion share the same goal, one Mirror Moment at a time,” said Connor Gibson, Dental Technology Manager, Remote Area Medical. RAM’s ongoing investment in mobile healthcare services reflects its commitment to reaching patients who face geographic, financial, or other obstacles to treatment. The addition of the NextDent 300 will further support that work, helping the organization’s dental teams provide essential restorative care through an increasingly efficient digital workflow. 3D Systems looks forward to continuing to support Remote Area Medical’s community outreach. For more information about 3D Systems’ NextDent Jetted Denture Solution, visit www.3dsystems.com . To learn more about Remote Area Medical and its mission to provide free healthcare to underserved communities, visit www.ramusa.org . About 3D Systems For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com . About Remote Area Medical Remote Area Medical (RAM®) is a nonprofit provider of free dental, vision, and medical services to underserved and uninsured individuals. Through its network of volunteers, pop-up clinics, and mobile healthcare units, RAM delivers essential care to individuals and communities in need, regardless of their ability to pay. For more information, visit www.ramusa.org .
